mainTopic: Sharpening and fixing tools on יום טוב, מכשירי אוכל נפש, rulings about skewers, רב מלכיו and רב מלכיא, and buying meat on יום טוב
overview: The גמרא finishes two matching stories about teachers who rubbed a knife on יום טוב. Each said he was only cleaning off the fat, but his student saw he was really sharpening it. This shows the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, but it is not taught publicly (הלכה ואין מורין כן). Next comes a debate about showing a knife to a חכם on יום טוב, and רב יוסף's rule that a dull knife may be sharpened if it still cuts with effort. Fixing a nicked knife, a crushed skewer, or sweeping out an oven all depend on the מחלוקת about מכשירי אוכל נפש. The גמרא explains each side's reading of the פסוק and concludes that רבי יהודה allows only preparations that could not have been done before יום טוב. Then come שמואל's rulings about bent and used skewers, a debate about moving a used skewer to a corner, and a side discussion telling רב מלכיו apart from רב מלכיא. Finally, a new משנה forbids asking a butcher for meat by price on יום טוב. The גמרא's explanation of how this is done continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The teacher who said he was only cleaning the knife
steps.stepSummary: A student sees his teacher rub a knife on a basket rim on יום טוב. The teacher says it is to remove fat, but the student sees he is really sharpening it. This shows the teacher holds הלכה ואין מורין כן.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He] was running the knife over the rim of a basket. I asked him: Are you doing this to sharpen it, or to remove its fat? He told me: To remove its fat. But I could see that he really meant to sharpen it. He holds that this is the הלכה, but we do not teach it to the public.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that began just before this section. A student watched his teacher sharpen a knife on יום טוב while saying he was only cleaning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sharpening a knife on יום טוב is the case where רבי יהודה is lenient. The teacher really did it, which shows he follows רבי יהודה. He hid this from his student because the leniency is not taught publicly, so that people will not take it too far.

keyTerms.meaning: Passing or running something over a surface
A basket made of palm branches
Its fat, meaning grease stuck on the knife
This is the law, but we do not rule this way publicly

steps.confusionAlert: The teacher was not being dishonest about the הלכה. He really holds it is allowed. He just did not want to give a public ruling, so he gave an answer that was also true, since rubbing the knife does remove the fat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea of הלכה ואין מורין כן: a true leniency that a teacher may act on himself but does not announce.

phrases.english: [he was] running the knife over the rim of a basket,
and I said to him:
Is the Master doing this to sharpen it,
or to remove its fat?
And he said to me: To remove its fat.
And I saw his real intention,
that he was doing it to sharpen it,
and he holds: it is the halacha, but we do not rule this way.
phrases.notes: He means the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, who allows sharpening, but we don't teach that to the public.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲזֵיתִי לְדַעְתֵּיהּ דִּלְחַדְּדָהּ קָא עָבֵיד, וְקָסָבַר: הֲלָכָה, וְאֵין מוֹרִין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began before this section, showing how a teacher actually behaved.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה, but is not ruled publicly
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teacher's own conduct of sharpening the knife on יום טוב while describing it as removing fat

steps.title: אביי tells the same kind of story about his teacher
steps.stepSummary: אביי saw his teacher rub a knife on the edge of a millstone on יום טוב. The teacher said it was to remove fat, but אביי saw he was really sharpening it. Again: הלכה ואין מורין כן.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I was standing before my Master, and he was running a knife over the edge of a millstone. I asked him: Do you want to sharpen it, or to remove its fat? He told me: To remove its fat. But I saw he really meant to sharpen it. He holds that this is the הלכה, but we do not teach it publicly.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells a second story that matches the first one almost word for word, this time about his own teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the knife is rubbed on the edge of a millstone instead of a basket rim. The lesson is the same: the teacher acts on רבי יהודה's leniency himself but keeps it quiet. A second story makes the point stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: I was standing before my Master

steps.whatToRemember: Two great teachers privately sharpened knives on יום טוב while giving a cleaning reason. The leniency of רבי יהודה is the הלכה, but it is not taught publicly.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
I was standing before my Master,
and he was running a knife
over the edge of a millstone.
And I said to him:
Does the Master want to sharpen it,
or to remove its fat?
And he said to me: To remove its fat.
And I saw his real intention,
that he was doing it to sharpen it,
and he holds: it is the halacha, but we do not rule this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story that backs up the same conclusion as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי יהודה but is not ruled publicly
steps.raayaSupportSource: The conduct of אביי's teacher, רבה, sharpening a knife on a millstone on יום טוב

steps.title: May one show a knife to a sage on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether, on יום טוב, one may bring a שחיטה knife to a חכם so he can check it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What is the law about showing a knife to a חכם on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It sets up the next steps, where different opinions will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, a knife must be checked for nicks, and a חכם was often asked to do this. The concern is that checking knives in front of people on יום טוב looks like a regular weekday activity.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the sages
To show, so that it can be checked

phrases.english: It was asked of them:

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְהַרְאוֹת סַכִּין לְחָכָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב?
phrases.english: What is the law about showing a knife to a sage on a Festival?
phrases.notes: He means a שחיטה knife, brought so the sage can check it for nicks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ לְהַרְאוֹת סַכִּין לְחָכָם בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from sharpening a knife to a related question: getting a knife checked on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one may show a שחיטה knife to a חכם for checking on יום טוב

steps.title: One sage permits, the רבנן forbid
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי בריה דרב ביזנא allowed showing the knife to a חכם, and the רבנן forbade it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי the son of רב ביזנא permitted it, and the רבנן forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a disagreement: one sage says it is allowed, and the רבנן say it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those who permit see it as a normal part of preparing food on יום טוב. The רבנן forbid it because a public knife inspection looks like a weekday activity.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages, here the majority opinion

phrases.aramaic: רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיזְנָא שָׁרֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Mari, son of Rav Bizna, permitted it,
and the Rabbis forbade it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב בִּיזְנָא שָׁרֵי, וְרַבָּנַן אָסְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 with two opposing views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב מרי בריה דרב ביזנא permits it; the רבנן forbid it.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the sage checks it privately and lends it out
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says a תלמיד חכם may check a knife for himself and then lend it to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: A תלמיד חכם checks a knife for himself and lends it to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a middle path between the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not bring knives to the חכם in public, which would look like weekday business. Instead the חכם checks his own knife at home and lends it to others. That way people still get a checked knife.
steps.whatToRemember: Showing a knife to a חכם on יום טוב is disputed. רב יוסף's solution: the חכם checks his own knife privately and lends it out.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
A Torah scholar examines [a knife] for himself,
and lends it to others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם רוֹאֶה לְעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer that sits between the lenient and strict views of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A חכם checks a knife privately for himself and then lends it to others.

steps.title: A dull knife may be sharpened if it still cuts with effort
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rules that a knife that has gone dull may be sharpened on יום טוב, but only if it still cuts with difficulty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף also said: A knife that has gone dull may be sharpened on יום טוב. This applies only when it still cuts, with effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב יוסף about sharpening a dull knife, and then limits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the knife still cuts, even with effort, sharpening only improves a working tool. If it no longer cuts at all, sharpening would be like making a new tool, and that stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: That has gone dull, literally that has 'stopped'

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general permission to sharpen any knife. It covers only a knife that still cuts. A knife that cannot cut at all may not be sharpened.
steps.whatToRemember: A dull knife may be sharpened on יום טוב only if it still cuts, even with effort.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
A knife that has become dull —
it is permitted to sharpen it on a Festival.
And this applies only
where it still cuts, with difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: סַכִּין שֶׁעָמְדָה מוּתָּר לְחַדְּדָהּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from the same speaker, רב יוסף, returning to the topic of sharpening knives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dull knife may be sharpened on יום טוב, but only if it still cuts, even with difficulty.

steps.title: Three tool-fixing cases depend on one dispute
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא (or רב יוסף) says three cases depend on the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and the רבנן: a nicked knife, a crushed skewer, and sweeping out an oven or stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא taught (some say it was רב יוסף): a knife that got nicked, a skewer that got crushed, and sweeping out an oven or stove on יום טוב all bring us to the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching groups three practical cases together. It says that whether they are allowed depends on a known disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these three acts is cooking itself. Each one gets a tool or oven ready so cooking can happen. That is why the answer depends on whether such preparations are allowed on יום טוב, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: sweeping the coals out of an oven

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda taught, and some say it was Rav Yosef:
Whether a knife that became nicked,
or a skewer that was crushed,
phrases.notes: Its point got bent or broken, so fixing it means straightening it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד גְּרִיפַת תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: or sweeping out an oven and a stove on a Festival —
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב חִסְדָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the discussion of sharpening a knife from step 6 into a general rule about fixing tools on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fixing a nicked knife, a crushed skewer, or sweeping an oven on יום טוב depends on the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא that holds the dispute
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is אוכל נפש. רבי יהודה also allows מכשירי אוכל נפש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: the only difference between יום טוב and שבת is making food. רבי יהודה also allows the things that prepare the way for making food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the מחלוקת that step 7 mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא allows only the actual making of food, such as cooking or slaughtering. רבי יהודה also allows the steps that make food-making possible, like fixing a knife. The three cases from step 7 belong to that second group.

keyTerms.meaning: things that prepare the way for making food

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אֵין בֵּין יוֹם טוֹב לַשַּׁבָּת
phrases.english: As it is taught: there is no difference between a Festival and Shabbat
except food preparation alone.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר אַף מַכְשִׁירֵי אוֹכֶל נֶפֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda permits even things that make food preparation possible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source of the מחלוקת named in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The existence and wording of the מחלוקת
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: אין בין יום טוב לשבת אלא אוכל נפש בלבד

steps.title: Why does the first תנא forbid preparations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the תנא קמא, who forbids preparations. This line sets up the next step, which gives his פסוק and then רבי יהודה's as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know which פסוק each side builds on. It starts with the stricter view, which forbids מכשירין.

keyTerms.meaning: the first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for each side of the מחלוקת

steps.title: Each side reads a different word in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns from the word הוא, "only it," and not its preparations. רבי יהודה learns from the word לכם, "for you," meaning all your needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, "only it may be done for you." The word "it" means only the food-making itself, not its preparations. רבי יהודה says the פסוק also says "for you," which means for all your needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that both sides learn from the same פסוק, but each one focuses on a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוא limits the permission to the food-making itself. The word לכם widens the permission to anything you need for food. This raises the next question: what does each side do with the other side's word?

phrases.english: The verse says: "Only it may be done for you."
"It" — and not the things that prepare for it.
And Rabbi Yehuda: the verse says, "for you,"
"for you" — for all your needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 for both sides.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא learns from הוא, not its preparations. רבי יהודה learns from לכם, all your needs.

steps.title: What does the first תנא do with "for you"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא: the פסוק also says לכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא, doesn't the פסוק also say "for you"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the תנא קמא, because he seems to ignore the word לכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לכם means "all your needs," it should include preparations. The תנא קמא has to explain what the word teaches according to him.

phrases.english: And the first tanna — isn't it written "for you"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יהודה's word to challenge the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא קמא's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word לכם seems to widen the permission, so it is hard to see how the תנא קמא can ignore it.

steps.title: "For you" and not for non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא explains that לכם means for Jews, not for גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: "for you" means for you and not for non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The תנא קמא answers that the word לכם teaches something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives לכם a different job. It limits who you may cook for on יום טוב, not what kind of work is allowed. So it does not widen the permission to preparations.

phrases.english: He would tell you:
That word, "for you" — and not for non-Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the תנא קמא has no use for לכם, so it must mean 'all your needs,' including preparations, as רבי יהודה reads it.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with "it"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה: the פסוק also says הוא, which limits the permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too, doesn't the פסוק say "it"?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the same challenge against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוא seems to rule out preparations. רבי יהודה has to explain how he can still allow them.

phrases.english: And the other one too — isn't it written "it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 11, this time against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word הוא limits the permission and seems to exclude preparations.

steps.title: Before יום טוב or not possible before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the two words as two cases. הוא forbids preparations that could have been done before יום טוב. לכם allows preparations that could not have been done before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: "it" is written and "for you" is written, and there is no contradiction. One word is about preparations that could have been done the day before יום טוב, and the other is about preparations that could not have been done the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה keeps both words by giving each one its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's permission is narrower than it first looked. He allows only the preparations you had no way of doing before יום טוב. This fits the three cases of step 7: the knife or skewer broke on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: from the day before יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא allows only food-making itself on יום טוב. רבי יהודה also allows preparations, but only those that could not have been done before יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not allow every preparation. If it could have been done the day before, even he forbids it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This limit is the key to the cases of step 7. Fixing a tool that broke on יום טוב is the kind of preparation that could not have been done earlier.

phrases.english: He would tell you: "it" is written,
and "for you" is written, and there is no difficulty:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּמַכְשִׁירִין שֶׁאֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: here, it is about preparations that can be done on the eve of the Festival,
phrases.notes: This is the word "it," which forbids these.

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּמַכְשִׁירִין שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹתָן מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: there, it is about preparations that cannot be done on the eve of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: כְּתִיב ״הוּא״, וּכְתִיב ״לָכֶם״, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two words into two different cases
steps.terutzMaskana: הוא excludes only preparations that could have been done before יום טוב. לכם allows those that could not.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה allows only preparations that could not have been done before יום טוב.

steps.title: A bent skewer may not be fixed on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a roasting skewer that got bent may not be straightened on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: if a skewer got bent, you may not fix it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל: you may not repair a bent roasting skewer on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skewer is a tool used to prepare food, not food itself. שמואל rules that fixing such a tool on יום טוב is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A skewer that became bent
it is forbidden to fix it on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute about preparations for food on יום טוב to a practical ruling about fixing a cooking tool.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bent skewer may not be repaired on יום טוב.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say this, since fixing a tool on יום טוב is clearly forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions שמואל's ruling: why say something everyone already knows?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repairing a utensil on יום טוב is a well-known prohibition. So the גמרא wants to know what new point שמואל is teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא asks why a ruling even needed to be said.

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for שמואל's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a bent skewer may not be fixed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fixing a tool on יום טוב is already known to be forbidden, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Forbidden even when it can be straightened by hand
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a skewer that can be straightened by hand. Even then, fixing it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed: even though it can be straightened by hand, it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל is teaching about an easy repair, one done by hand with no tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a quick fix by hand doesn't count as real repair work. שמואל teaches that it is still forbidden on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for a special case
It can be straightened by hand

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think a 'small' repair done by hand is allowed. The whole point of the ruling is that even this easy fix is forbidden.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary,
for even though it can be straightened by hand.
phrases.notes: The ending is left out but understood: even so, it is still forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא of step 16 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A repair done easily by hand, with no tool, might be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a hand-straightening repair of a skewer is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: A used skewer may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a skewer already used to roast meat may not be moved on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה also said in the name of שמואל: a skewer that meat was roasted on may not be moved on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ruling of שמואל about a skewer: once it has been used for roasting, it is off-limits to move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the roasting, the skewer has finished its job and has no other use that day. So it is treated as מוקצה and may not be handled.

keyTerms.meaning: To move it or carry it
Something set apart that may not be moved on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A skewer on which they roasted meat
it is forbidden to move it on Yom Tov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same speakers about the same object, the skewer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A skewer used for roasting may not be moved on יום טוב.

steps.title: Pull it out and put it in a corner
steps.stepSummary: רב מלכיו allows pulling the skewer out and putting it in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב מלכיו: one may pull it out and put it in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מלכיו adds a permission: even though the skewer is not normally moved, you may slide it out and put it aside in a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sharp skewer lying around the house can hurt someone. So רב מלכיו allows moving it out of the way, into a corner.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulls it out (from the meat)

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav Malkiyu said:
He pulls it out and places it in a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב מַלְכִּיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to שמואל's ban on moving the skewer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The used skewer may be pulled out and set aside in a corner.

steps.title: Only when an olive-size of meat is still on it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits רב מלכיו's permission to a skewer with at least a כזית of meat on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב הונא: this applies only when there is a כזית of meat on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא narrows רב מלכיו's permission: you may move the skewer only if some meat, a כזית, is still on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meat is food, and food may be moved. So the skewer can be moved because of the meat on it. Without that meat, the skewer stays off-limits.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said that Rav Huna said:
And this is when there is an olive-bulk of meat on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The skewer may be moved to a corner only if a כזית of meat remains on it.

steps.title: Even with no meat, like a thorn in the street
steps.stepSummary: רבינא allows moving the skewer even with no meat on it, comparing it to removing a thorn from the public street.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: even if there is no meat on it, it may be moved, just like a thorn lying in the public domain.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא disagrees with רב הונא and allows moving the skewer to a corner even when no meat is left on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים allowed moving a thorn out of a public street so people won't get hurt. רבינא says the same safety reason lets you move a dangerous skewer, even without meat on it.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two views on רב מלכיו's permission to move a used skewer to a corner. רב הונא allows it only if a כזית of meat is on it. רבינא allows it even with no meat, because of safety, like a thorn in the street.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו בָּשָׂר
phrases.english: Even though there is no meat on it
it is permitted to move it,
just as with a thorn in the public domain.
phrases.notes: A thorn lying in the street could hurt people, so moving it out of the way is allowed. The danger is the reason.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עָלָיו בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא's limit in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A used skewer may be moved to a corner even with no meat on it, for safety, like a thorn in the public domain.

steps.title: Three rulings that come from רב מלכיו
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא lists three rulings that belong to רב מלכיו: the skewer, the maidservants, and the follicles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא son of רב איקא said: the rulings about the skewer, maidservants, and follicles are from רב מלכיו.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב מלכיו was just quoted, the גמרא adds a side note: a list of three rulings that come from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a memory list that tells us which rulings are רב מלכיו's. The skewer ruling is the one we just learned. The other two, about maidservants and about follicles, are rulings taught in other places.

keyTerms.meaning: Small hollows (hair follicles), a sign of physical maturity

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Hinnana son of Rav Ika said:
Skewer, maidservants, and follicles
phrases.notes: These are short names for three rulings. Only the skewer one is from our page; the other two are taught elsewhere.

phrases.english: are Rav Malkiyu's.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note on who said what, prompted by the mention of רב מלכיו in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rulings of the skewer, the maidservants, and the follicles all belong to רב מלכיו.

steps.title: The other three rulings belong to רב מלכיא
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא finishes his list: the rulings about the forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese were said by a different sage, רב מלכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese: these were said by רב מלכיא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חיננא finishes his statement from the previous step. He names three other rulings that were not said by רב מלכיו but by a sage with a similar name, רב מלכיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two names, מלכיו and מלכיא, look almost the same, so people could mix them up. רב חיננא gives a fixed list: three rulings go to רב מלכיו (skewer, maidservants, follicles) and three go to רב מלכיא (forelock, burnt ashes, cheese).

keyTerms.meaning: A forelock, a lock of hair grown in front

steps.confusionAlert: רב מלכיא and רב מלכיו are two different people. Read the last letters of each name carefully.

phrases.english: The forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese
phrases.notes: Each word is short for a whole ruling: cutting a non-Jew's forelock, putting ashes on a wound, and cheese made by non-Jews.

phrases.english: were said by רב מלכיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּלוֹרִית, אֵפֶר מִקְלֶה, וּגְבִינָה — רַב מַלְכִּיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רב חיננא's list, which began in step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The forelock, burnt ashes, and cheese rulings belong to רב מלכיא, not רב מלכיו.

steps.title: רב פפא's rule for telling the two sages apart
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that comments on a משנה or ברייתא come from רב מלכיא, and stand-alone rulings come from רב מלכיו. His memory aid is 'the משנה is a queen'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Comments on a משנה or a ברייתא were said by רב מלכיא. Stand-alone rulings were said by רב מלכיו. Your memory aid: the משנה is a queen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different way to sort the rulings. He does not use a list. He uses a general rule based on what kind of teaching it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ruling explains a משנה or ברייתא, it belongs to רב מלכיא. If it is an independent ruling, it belongs to רב מלכיו. The memory aid works because מלכיא sounds like מלכתא, 'queen', and the משנה is called a queen.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
Comments on a משנה or a ברייתא were said by רב מלכיא.
Stand-alone rulings were said by רב מלכיו.
And your memory aid: the משנה is a queen.
phrases.notes: מלכתא, 'queen', sounds like מלכיא, so the queen (the משנה) goes with רב מלכיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַתְנִיתִין וּמַתְנִיתָא — רַב מַלְכִּיָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way to divide the rulings than רב חיננא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Teachings on a משנה or ברייתא belong to רב מלכיא; stand-alone rulings belong to רב מלכיו.

steps.title: Where do רב חיננא and רב פפא disagree?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב חיננא's list and רב פפא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which ruling each view would assign to a different sage. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views mostly assign the rulings the same way. The גמרא wants to find the specific ruling where the two methods give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two views just given
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ruling is assigned differently by רב חיננא and רב פפא

steps.title: They differ on the maidservants ruling
steps.stepSummary: The difference is the ruling about maidservants. רב חיננא gives it to רב מלכיו, but by רב פפא's rule it goes to רב מלכיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: the maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views split over the maidservants ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חיננא listed the maidservants ruling under רב מלכיו. That ruling is a comment on a משנה, so רב פפא's rule would assign it to רב מלכיא.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: רב חיננא sorts the rulings by a fixed list, and רב פפא sorts them by type. Only the maidservants ruling comes out differently.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: the maidservants.
phrases.notes: This is the maidservants ruling from רב חיננא's list in the previous steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The maidservants ruling: רב מלכיו according to רב חיננא, רב מלכיא according to רב פפא

steps.title: משנה: Do not ask the butcher for a דינר's worth of meat
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב a person may not ask a butcher to weigh out a דינר's worth of meat. But the butcher may slaughter an animal and divide it among people.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may not say to a butcher: 'Weigh out for me a דינר's worth of meat.' But the butcher may slaughter an animal and divide it among them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches how people may get meat from a butcher on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming a price makes it look like a normal business deal, which is not allowed on יום טוב. Slaughtering an animal and sharing it out, without mentioning money, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin of a set value

phrases.english: משנה:
A person may not say to a butcher:
'Weigh out for me a דינר's worth of meat,'
phrases.notes: This is talking about יום טוב, when naming a price looks like doing business.

phrases.english: but he may slaughter and divide it among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַטַּבָּח: שְׁקוֹל לִי בְּדִינָר בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not ask for meat by price, but the butcher may slaughter and divide the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that on יום טוב you may get food, but not in a way that looks like buying and selling.

steps.title: How is it done in practice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how someone can take a share of the meat if he is not allowed to mention its price.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: How does one do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a practical question about the משנה. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids naming a price but allows dividing the animal. The גמרא wants to know how the sharing can work without talking about money.

phrases.english: גמרא:
How does one do it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to carry out the משנה's permission
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a person can take a share of the meat without naming a price

steps.title: The answer begins: like this case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts its answer by pointing to a case. The details continue in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in this case...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering with 'כי הא', meaning 'like this case'. It is setting up an example that continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a rule, the גמרא is about to show the answer through an actual case or practice.

phrases.english: As in this case

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 28
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer will be given through an example case, which continues in the next lines
